key_insight: Block-landmark scoring makes attention sparse enough for full KV to live off-HBM; at 1M tokens a 70B GQA model needs ~330 GB of KV per sequence.
killer_doubt: Fetching 32 blocks x 64 tokens x 320 KB (70B GQA) is 0.67 GB per decode step: ~48 ms on a 14 GB/s SSD, ~200 pJ/bit versus HBM ~3.5.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. To size it, run Quest/InfLLM-style top-k with KV on a 4x Gen5 SSD array versus CPU-DRAM offload at 128k-1M tokens (RULER), reporting tokens/s per sequence, SSD DWPD and J/token. ~$30k.
prior_art: Landmark Attention (2023), Quest (ICML 2024), InfLLM, ShadowKV, RetrievalAttention, InstInfer in-SSD attention, CachedAttention SSD KV store (from memory).

key_insight: Tree topology at ~2n bits versus ~128n for pointers is a large cut; an engine that chains rank-directory and bitvector reads inside the controller attacks succinctness's real cost, dependent misses.
killer_doubt: x86 POPCNT/PDEP already do in-word rank/select in ~3 cycles; cost is 2-4 dependent ~100 ns DRAM misses per hop, and the controller saves only ~30-50 ns of fabric each.
decisive_experiment: Build a rank/select/balanced-parentheses unit on an FPGA CXL memory expander (~$20k board); run LOUDS trie, BP tree and Elias-Fano graph BFS against pointer and SDSL-software versions. Continue only if within 1.5x pointer latency at 5x less memory.
prior_art: SDSL-lite and Succinct (NSDI 2015) in software; SpZip (ISCA 2021) near-core graph decompression; FM-index rank accelerators and PIM for genomics, e.g. MEDAL (from memory).

key_insight: Profile-guided choice of data-structure representation could shrink read-mostly maps and graphs without programmer effort; succinct encodings are the right target for cold indexes.
killer_doubt: Rank/select instructions largely exist (x86 POPCNT+PDEP+TZCNT, ARM SVE2 BDEP/BEXT); swapping mutable containers needs proven read-only phases, so coverage is likely <10% of heap.
decisive_experiment: Census five production-like services (search index, KV store, BWA genomics, graph DB, ads) for the heap share held in read-mostly maps and trees; kill if under 15%. ~$20k of engineering.
prior_art: Data-structure selection tools: Chameleon (PLDI 2009), Brainy (PLDI 2011), CollectionSwitch (CGO 2018); SDSL; BMI2 and SVE2 bit-permute instructions (from memory).

key_insight: Static-camera and screen streams are temporally redundant, so storing only changed-token KV with back-references fits streaming video LLMs, whose KV grows linearly with frame count.
killer_doubt: Prior art already drops ~80% of redundant video tokens; deep-layer KV of an unchanged patch still differs (context mixing, RoPE position), and merged tokens need softmax count bias.
decisive_experiment: On a 7B video LLM, compare per-layer thresholded KV dedup with input-side run-length tokenization at equal KV memory on hour-long static-camera and screen-recording streams, scoring streaming QA accuracy. ~$20k GPU.
prior_art: Run-Length Tokenization (NeurIPS 2024); TimeChat-Online differential token drop (2025); ToMe proportional attention; StreamingVLM, Flash-VStream (from memory).

key_insight: 3^5 = 243 <= 256 packs ternary at 1.6 bits per weight, 99% of the 1.585-bit entropy bound; native ternary training makes the packing lossless.
killer_doubt: Already shipped: llama.cpp TQ1_0 packs five trits per byte (~1.69 bpw) and bitnet.cpp uses LUT kernels. Against today's 4-bit deployment the gain is 2.5x, not 10x.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. Benchmark public ternary checkpoints (BitNet b1.58 2B4T) against 4-bit-quantized models of equal weight memory on standard evals and tokens/s. ~$10k.
prior_art: BitNet b1.58 (Microsoft 2024) and 2B4T (2025); llama.cpp TQ1_0/TQ2_0 formats; bitnet.cpp TL1/TL2 lookup kernels (from memory).

key_insight: Zero-skipping saves compute energy on adder-only hardware; for memory, the only question is whether zero runs carry entropy below the 1.585-bit ternary bound.
killer_doubt: At ~40% zeros ternary entropy is 1.57 bits per weight, so run-length coding saves ~2% over five-trit packing; zeros must exceed ~80% (H = 0.92) to matter.
decisive_experiment: Histogram zero fraction and run lengths in BitNet b1.58 2B4T weights, then compute empirical entropy against 1.6 bpw. One day of scripting, <$1k.
prior_art: Same packing as I-06286 (BitNet, TQ1_0); zero-skipping in EIE (ISCA 2016) and Cambricon-X; ternary keyword-spotting accelerators (from memory).

key_insight: Coarse codes in DRAM with refinement from flash is the right hierarchy for vector indexes: 4-bit or PQ codes need 8-100x less DRAM, and flash serves only reranks.
killer_doubt: This is already standard practice: DiskANN keeps ~32 B PQ codes per vector in DRAM with full vectors on SSD, and FAISS refine plus Matryoshka/residual quantization do coarse-then-fine.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. Benchmark against DiskANN on BigANN-100M at equal recall@10 and QPS; continue only if DRAM falls a further >1.5x. ~$10k.
prior_art: DiskANN (NeurIPS 2019), SPANN (NeurIPS 2021), FAISS IndexRefine/IVFPQ, Matryoshka representations (NeurIPS 2022), residual quantization (from memory).

key_insight: 4 KB pages compress poorly for lack of context; a shared trained dictionary supplies that context, and pinning it in compressor SRAM makes it free per page.
killer_doubt: Linux zram already accepts zstd dictionaries. Dictionary gain on 4 KB pages is likely ~10-30%, and compressed tiers hold ~20-30% of memory, so net DRAM saved is ~2-8%.
decisive_experiment: Train zstd dictionaries on page samples from JVM, Python and embedding workloads; measure the 4 KB-page ratio with and without a dictionary across a week of drift. Kill if gain <20%. ~$10k.
prior_art: zstd dictionary training (Meta); Linux zram zstd/lz4 dictionary support (~v6.12, from memory); Intel IAA canned Huffman tables; TMO/zswap far memory.

key_insight: KV energy concentrates at low frequency along the token axis, so transform coding plus per-head quantization tables can stack on plain quantization. Pre-RoPE keys correlate best.
killer_doubt: FreqKV (ICLR 2026) already applies DCT along the sequence dimension. The baseline is wrong: 2-bit KIVI already gives ~8x versus FP16, so a transform must beat ~2 bits/element.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. To size the residual gain on Llama-3-8B, compare FreqKV plus 2-bit quantization against KIVI-2 at equal bits on LongBench/RULER; continue only if >1.5x smaller at equal accuracy. ~$10k GPU.
prior_art: FreqKV (arXiv 2505.00570, ICLR 2026) DCT along sequence (via search snippet); CacheGen (SIGCOMM 2024) token-delta coding; KIVI, KVQuant pre-RoPE keys (from memory).

key_insight: Frozen weights need no endurance or refresh. Workaround: a capacitor-less DRAM array whose storage-node contact is the programming via, giving DRAM density, non-destructive read and no read disturb.
killer_doubt: HBF claims 8-16x HBM capacity at similar cost; a single-level 6F2 ROM saves only ~20-30% of DRAM wafer cost (no capacitor), so it loses ~5x on $/bit.
decisive_experiment: Run an accelerated read-disturb test on commercial 3D TLC and SLC-mode NAND (~1e4 reads/s per block) to find HBF's rewrite interval at 20-50 weight reads/s. Add a step-count cost model of capacitor-less DRAM-array ROM. ~$80k.
prior_art: Taalas HC1 mask-ROM weights on TSMC N6 (via search snippet, earlier logs); Sandisk/SK hynix HBF OCP spec 2026; contact/via mask ROM; sibling ideas I-00502, I-04289.

key_insight: Passive optical splitting delivers one weight stream to N accelerators. Receive-only energy of ~0.5-1 pJ/bit could undercut local HBM reads (~3.5 pJ/bit), making weights a shared broadcast resource.
killer_doubt: Each GPU needs its shard every step: 405 GB/8 GPUs at 20 steps/s is ~1 TB/s ingress. Wide-EP NVL72 serving already holds weights at ~5% of HBM.
decisive_experiment: Simulate layer-locked continuous batching on vLLM traces to measure throughput lost to carousel phase alignment. Build a 1:16 passive-split 4x100G FPGA link demo measuring delivered pJ/bit. ~$400k.
prior_art: Cerebras weight streaming (MemoryX/SwarmX broadcast to CS-2, for training); NVLink SHARP multicast; DSM-CC and teletext data carousels (from memory).

key_insight: A content-hash census across page cache, socket buffers, heaps and GPU staging shows where duplicate copies persist, turning zero-copy work into measured DRAM savings.
killer_doubt: In-flight copies live microseconds: at 10 GB/s and ~100 us residency only ~1 MB is duplicated. Persistent duplication (DB buffer pool plus page cache) is already fixed by O_DIRECT.
decisive_experiment: Run the eBPF/page-hash census on 20 storage, proxy and ingest nodes for a week and report persistent duplicate GB per node. Kill if <5% of DRAM. ~$30k of engineering.
prior_art: KSM and VM dedup studies (Difference Engine, OSDI 2008); io_uring registered buffers, splice, MSG_ZEROCOPY; O_DIRECT double-caching fixes; bpftrace/drgn profilers (from memory).
